title: Approve the artifact
lesson: Bind human approval to the exact proposed artifact, and require fresh review when an agent changes it before execution.
limitations: Illustrative executor; no framework or prompt automatically guarantees artifact-bound authorization.
A/B abbreviate immutable artifact identities; target binding, authenticated decisions, race protection and retry handling are outside this cut.
Human review and testing durations are compressed, not benchmarks.
Audio was analysed, not physically listened to.
Self-reviewed; independent comparative review and default promotion remain separate.

transcript.text: An agent runs tests and prepares release artifact A. Production remains unchanged behind a closed execution gate.
A reviewer inspects A and approves that artifact. The approval is recorded separately; nothing has deployed yet.
The agent prepares revision B. The executor compares B with approval for A, detects a mismatch and keeps production unchanged. The old approval is stale.
B returns to the reviewer. A fresh approval for B replaces the stale one, and the executor waits to recheck the pair.
The executor matches B to its new approval, opens the gate and releases B. This illustrates an enforced approval boundary; the scene fades to its opening state.
